passage: Xin's thumb hovered over the screen on the tram home through Copenhagen. Three texts to Anders since lunch, and not one from him. The fourth was typed: "Are you ignoring me?" She deleted it, put the phone face down on her knee and breathed slowly until the tram reached her stop. At home she wrote a different message: "Honestly, when I don't hear back, I get scared you're losing interest. Could you just send a quick 'busy' when you are?" Then she went to choir practice, where she had a solo to learn, and forgot to check her phone for an hour. When she looked, Anders had replied: "Sorry, football ran late. Yes, I can do that. Sing well."

qa.q: What did Xin's fourth text say before she deleted it?
qa.a: It said, "Are you ignoring me?"

qa.q: What was Xin worried about when Anders didn't reply?
qa.a: She was scared that Anders was losing interest, and she named that fear in her new message.

qa.q: What was the turning point on the tram, and why did it help?
qa.a: She deleted the fourth text and breathed until her stop, which gave her time to calm down and ask clearly instead of accusing.

qa.q: How might Anders have felt reading the calm request instead of "Are you ignoring me?"
qa.a: He probably found it easy to say yes, since it asked for something simple rather than blaming him.

grounding: A teenager stops before a fourth text, names her fear, asks plainly for what she needs and turns to her own interest in singing.

passage:
In the school counsellor's room, Himani sat twisting her ID card strap. "Rekha's always with the new basketball girls now. I've messaged her three times since yesterday."
"And a fourth is waiting?" the counsellor asked.
Himani laughed shakily. "Typed already."
"What's the fear under it?"
Himani was quiet. "That I'll have nobody if she drifts."
"That's a real fear. What could you ask her for, directly?"
"Maybe... one lunch a week, just us."
She sent that instead of the fourth text. On the way out she stopped at the notice board and wrote her name on the sign-up sheet for the Saturday pottery club. Rekha's reply came before the bell: "Wednesday lunches? Yes!!"

qa.q: Which club did Himani sign up for?
qa.a: She signed up for the Saturday pottery club.

qa.q: What was Himani afraid of underneath the urge to send a fourth text?
qa.a: She feared she would have nobody if Rekha drifted away.

qa.q: Which choice changed the outcome, and why?
qa.a: Himani asked Rekha directly for one lunch a week instead of sending a fourth message, which gave Rekha something easy to say yes to.

qa.q: How might Rekha have seen a clear request for lunch compared with many worried messages?
qa.a: She likely found it easy and welcome, which shows in her eager reply.

grounding: With a counsellor's questions, a teenager pauses before a fourth message, names her fear, asks her friend directly and joins a club of her own.

passage:
Dear Harsha,
You asked how things are with Vikram, so here's the honest version. Last Tuesday he didn't reply all evening. I had three texts sent and a fourth typed: "Fine, forget it." My thumb was on send. Then I did the thing we used to laugh about in Class 9: I wrote down what I was actually scared of. "That I'm not important to him." Seeing it on paper made it smaller. I deleted the fourth text. Next day I told him, "When you vanish, I get scared. Can you tell me if you're busy?" He said yes, easily. Also, I've rejoined the basketball team, and my Saturdays are mine again. Write back soon.
Ankita

qa.q: What did the fourth text say?
qa.a: "Fine, forget it."

qa.q: What was Ankita afraid of under the urge to send the fourth text?
qa.a: Ankita was scared of not being important to Vikram, and writing it down made the fear feel smaller.

qa.q: Which steps did Ankita take that worked?
qa.a: Pausing, naming the fear on paper, deleting the angry text and asking Vikram directly to say when busy.

qa.q: How might Vikram feel getting a clear request instead of an angry fourth text?
qa.a: He probably feels relieved and more willing to help, since he could agree easily instead of defending himself.

grounding: Shows a teen pausing before a fourth text, naming the fear, asking directly and building a life beyond one relationship.

passage: People think this only happens with girlfriends. For me it was my best friend, Keerthana. I'm Wasim, Class 11, and last year if she didn't answer by lunch I'd assume she'd dropped me for the debate crowd. Message after message. One day I had three unanswered and was typing a fourth, something sarcastic, when my sister said, "Put it down. What are you actually scared of?" I said, "That she doesn't need me." Saying it out loud felt silly, and also lighter. So I asked Keerthana straight: "Are we okay? I get jumpy when you go quiet." She laughed and said her phone had been taken in class. Since then I've joined the photography club. It helps to have more than one person in my world.

qa.q: What was Wasim typing when the sister spoke?
qa.a: A fourth message, something sarcastic.

qa.q: How did Wasim feel after saying the fear out loud?
qa.a: Wasim felt silly but also lighter, because naming the fear took away some of its power.

qa.q: What would you advise someone in Wasim's place, based on what worked?
qa.a: Pause before the next message, name the fear and ask the friend directly, while also building other friendships and interests.

qa.q: How does Keerthana seem to react to Wasim's direct question?
qa.a: Keerthana takes it lightly and laughs, explaining her phone was taken, which suggests the friendship was never in danger.

grounding: Illustrates a teen calming the alarm by pausing, naming the fear, asking directly and widening life beyond one friend.

passage: I'm Pankaj, and I share a wall with my cousin Amandeep, so I hear things. Last month, every evening, it was the ping-ping-ping of her messages to her boyfriend, then silence, then her pacing. Last Friday was different. Through the open door I saw her, phone in hand, thumb hovering. Then she put it face-down, picked up her guitar and played the same four chords for about ten minutes. Later I heard her on a call, quiet and clear: "When you don't reply, I start thinking the worst. Can we agree you'll say if you're busy?" I can't know exactly what she felt. But she came out for dinner smiling and asked me to come to her Sunday jam with her school friends.

qa.q: What did Amandeep pick up after putting the phone face-down?
qa.a: Her guitar.

qa.q: What might Amandeep have been feeling while her thumb hovered over the phone?
qa.a: She was probably anxious about the silence, but chose to calm herself before sending anything.

qa.q: What did Amandeep do that a teen in a similar spot could copy?
qa.a: Pause, soothe the panic with something absorbing, then ask the other person clearly for what is needed.

qa.q: How does Pankaj see the change in Amandeep?
qa.a: Pankaj notices the pacing replaced by calm, a clear call and a new interest in sharing her music with friends, without being sure what she felt.

grounding: Shows through an observer a teen pausing before texting, asking directly and turning to interests and friends.

passage:
Monday: Dolma hadn't replied since lunch. Ritu sent "?" then "hello??" then "are you mad at me". Her chest was tight all evening, and she couldn't focus on anything.
Thursday: Dolma was quiet again. Ritu's thumb hovered over a fourth message. She put the phone down and said out loud, "I'm scared she's pulling away." Then she typed one text: "Hey, I get worried when things go quiet. Can you tell me if we're okay?" Dolma replied an hour later: "We're fine!! Just exams."
Two weeks later: Ritu had joined the school pottery club on Wednesdays and started messaging Sonam from the club too. When Dolma went quiet on Sunday, Ritu noticed the worry, and went back to shaping her lopsided bowl.

qa.q: What club did Ritu join?
qa.a: The school pottery club on Wednesdays.

qa.q: What was Ritu afraid of on Thursday?
qa.a: She was scared that Dolma was pulling away from her, and she named that fear out loud before texting.

qa.q: Which step on Thursday worked, and why?
qa.a: Ritu paused instead of sending a fourth message, named the fear, and asked directly whether they were okay, which got a clear answer.

qa.q: What might Monday's messages have been like for Dolma?
qa.a: Dolma, busy with exams, might have felt pressured or confused by several worried texts in a row.

grounding: Shows a teen learning to pause before another text, name her fear, ask directly, and build other friendships and interests.
